title: Qwen Responds to the Rumors of Qwen Go! : The Experience Qualification for Non-Independent App is Now Open for Application

content_html:
Regarding various speculations about "Qwen Go!", the Qwen team made an official clarification on the same day through their official WeChat account: this product, named Personal Agent, is not an independent application available for download, but rather a personal AI agent embedded directly within the Qwen APP. A dedicated experience application entry has already been placed inside the APP, allowing users to submit applications. The official will gradually open access permissions to more people in batches.

In the announcement, Qwen reiterated that enabling everyone to have a personalized AI assistant has always been the team's goal. Previously, leveraging the Alibaba ecosystem and open platform, Qwen has already been able to assist users with tasks such as shopping, travel, and logistics in dozens of fields. The launch of "Qwen Go!" means that its scope and processing capabilities have taken a new step forward, allowing it to handle a wider range of personal tasks.

Tested: Can claim insurance and compare prices, received 70 yuan for flight delay

From the actual experience, the "hands-on ability" of this built-in assistant has already attracted attention. After testing, reporters found that users can use it to complete a series of tasks such as claiming flight delay compensation, booking venues and performances, selecting and reserving restaurants, comparing prices and placing orders, and even applying for jobs. In a test video, a user asked "Qwen Go!" to check if a flight was delayed and had it contact the platform customer service to file a claim, ultimately successfully receiving 70 yuan in compensation.

The Qwen team stated that the product will continue to collect real usage feedback and improve the experience, evolving toward a smarter and more personalized assistant that fits individual habits. At a time when major companies are pushing AI from a "question-answering tool" to an "agent that can accomplish tasks," Qwen chose to first implement it within existing apps instead of building an independent application, which is both stable and shows its intention to directly monetize its ecosystem capabilities.
